finding: The selected reference specs/request-consistency.md#requirements has no matching Input snapshot. The request contains 31 Inputs and none has filePath specs/request-consistency.md, so the selected requirement cannot be compared with the supplied snapshots. Its absence also leaves the immutable request and request-binding concepts that specs/promotion-runtime.md relies on unverifiable from the request, so readiness cannot be established for this selection.

The selected conditional export retention obligation applies only if the Reader Index Update target docs/reference/validation-report.md is a generated artifact; if it is a manually maintained document, the section does not apply. No supplied Input states which kind of document that target is. specs/reader-index.md names it only as the new link target, and architecture/05 states only that it already exists. The applicability of the 30-day ADR 0005 retention obligation therefore cannot be determined from the request.

The selected reference specs/image-cache.md#preview-cleanup is not a delivery requirement of this issue. What to build states that only the listed behaviors are delivered and that listing a requirement does not add delivery content. The listed items are Validation Report, Result Summary, invalid-input diagnostic wording, indexed cache lookup, single-scan parser strategy, protected access review, promotion, recovery, runtime migration and Reader Index Update. The cited section requires cleanup of documentation-renderer image previews after 24 hours, which none of these items defines or implements.

Both selected requirements define the caller-visible successful result of promote(inputPath), and they are incompatible. runtime-migration requires the successful result to be exactly {status, artifactId, trackedStateId}. result-summary requires promote to return a string summary in the existing structured result. The issue cannot satisfy both exact definitions.

runtime-migration fixes the Expected filesystem failure of promote to exactly {recovered, failureCode, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus} and then assigns the remaining failure semantics to Promotion Runtime. promotion-runtime's Failure Results, cited as the current comparison contract for the same caller-visible result, defines {recovered, failureCode, operation, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}, where operation identifies the failed step. The two exact field sets are incompatible, so the failure result cannot be implemented to satisfy both.

The request-binding requirement says Readiness must confirm that artifact.requestId equals immutable request.requestId and that inputPath equals the artifact path bound to the current request before calling persistence. It also says Promotion trusts this precondition and adds no public parameter or failure branch. No selected text defines the caller-visible result, or whether any write occurs, when that confirmation fails, and the stated Expected filesystem failure and rollback failure cases do not cover a binding mismatch. The outcome of the binding requirement is therefore undefined.

Retention Policy Ownership requires successful tracked artifacts to be kept for 30 days and states that removal after expiry is not part of the promote operation. It also says downstream persistence only consumes the applied selection. No selected text defines an observable effect of that 30-day selection, and no supplied Input assigns expiry or removal to an owner. ADR 0005 limits Readiness to applying the policy and does not assign expiry. The retention obligation therefore has no executing owner in the delivered scope.

The Authentication Boundary and Authorization Behavior requirements make the decision depend on the verified principal supplied by the existing caller boundary. The only caller-visible input the selected requirements define is the immutable request, with resourceId and operation as facts. No selected requirement names a principal input or describes how the principal reaches the operation. rules/01-required-inputs.md states that the existing caller boundary hands the review boundary the verified principal and the requested operation, so the selected input contract does not carry the principal that the current contract requires, and the principal-dependent decision cannot be implemented as written.

The Reader Index Update requirement assigns pre-publication verification of the removed old target and the single matching new target to a Documentation owner. No supplied Input defines that role. The subject's Acceptance criteria cover caller-visible behavior through public lifecycle verification and pure internal behavior through source review, so this documentation check is covered by no acceptance criterion. The selected requirement therefore has no defined verifier or completion check.
